title: How to Rewrite Apache Spark UDFs for GPU Acceleration with AI Agents | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA describes using coding agents with 'cuDF skills for Apache Spark' to rewrite CPU-bound Spark UDFs into GPU-native forms; a consumer-tech customer converted 30+ production UDFs, with one rewrite cutting operator time from 274.55 to 12.78 hours (22X) on a 600-billion-row workload. It is vendor content aimed at expanding GPU-accelerated Spark adoption.

themes.theme: UDFs as the barrier to GPU data analytics

insights.claim: Spark UDFs break the declarative SQL/DataFrame abstraction that lets the cuDF plugin parallelize transparently, forcing columnar-to-row conversion and CPU fallback row by row, which adds round-trip transfer overhead and forfeits GPU compute speedup.
insights.speaker: Rishi Chandra
insights.so_what: Opaque custom code is the main leak in GPU-accelerated Spark TCO; migrating UDFs is a prerequisite for NVIDIA's data-analytics savings claims.

insights.claim: Rewriting UDFs has long been laborious, requiring careful API selection, semantic validation and performance measurement, and columnar APIs are unfamiliar to many practitioners, which is the friction agents are meant to reduce.
insights.speaker: Rishi Chandra
insights.so_what: Engineering effort rather than hardware has been the adoption bottleneck for GPU Spark.

insights.claim: NVIDIA lays out three UDF rewrite approaches by complexity: Spark SQL expressions for simple relational logic, the RapidsUDF interface with the Java API for cuDF (evaluateColumnar) for most cases such as string parsing and nested types, and custom CUDA kernels via JNI for the most complex or performance-critical logic.
insights.speaker: Rishi Chandra
insights.so_what: Gives a decision ladder for migration effort; CUDA kernels deepen lock-in to NVIDIA's stack.
insights.locator: We outline three approaches to rewrite UDFs

insights.claim: With a small, targeted code change many UDFs can be made GPU-accelerable, eliminating fallback overhead and yielding speedups of over 20X.
insights.speaker: Rishi Chandra
insights.so_what: Vendor-stated upside that supports GPU-for-analytics TCO arguments.

insights.claim: Rewrites are suited to coding agents with guardrails: an agent can search unfamiliar APIs, implement candidates and iterate quickly while executable tests and performance measurements decide whether each change is acceptable.
insights.speaker: Rishi Chandra
insights.so_what: Verification-driven loops are the pattern that makes coding agents reliable for performance migration work.
insights.quote: With proper guardrails, an agent can search unfamiliar APIs

insights.claim: The cuDF skills for Apache Spark break the rewrite into four feedback loops (testing, conversion, benchmarking, optimization), each requiring evidence before the next stage, and ship a project template with test and benchmark harnesses, output-verification routines and build configuration so the agent is not rebuilding infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Rishi Chandra
insights.so_what: Encoding domain scaffolding into reusable agent skills is a template for vendors to drive adoption of their platforms.

insights.claim: The skills offer GPU-programming best practices as advisory tips rather than rigid rules, leaving the agent free to explore implementations and pick based on measured correctness and performance, which is meant to leverage frontier models.
insights.speaker: Rishi Chandra
insights.so_what: Signals a design preference for guided autonomy over scripted pipelines.
insights.locator: The skills also provide best practices

insights.claim: NVIDIA is distributing the workflow as installable agent skills (via an npx skill installer from GitHub) and the post notes it was powered by NVIDIA Nemotron for its summary, tying AI agents to its own software ecosystem.
insights.speaker: Rishi Chandra
insights.so_what: Agent skills are becoming a distribution channel for hardware vendors' software stacks.

insights.claim: A major consumer technology company converted more than 30 production UDFs with the workflow, and one rewrite cut operator time from 274.55 to 12.78 hours (22X) across a 600-billion-row workload; that UDF affected more than 3,000 jobs and rewrites preserved original behavior.
insights.speaker: Rishi Chandra
insights.so_what: Single customer-supplied case study; the 3,000-job footprint suggests large fleet-wide savings if generalized.
insights.quote: Rewriting a production CPU-based UDF with cuDF reduced operator time from 274.55 to 12.78 hours

insights.claim: Agents let practitioners iterate on UDF rewrites in hours rather than days or weeks without compromising correctness, per NVIDIA, making GPU Spark conversion cheaper to scale.
insights.speaker: Rishi Chandra
insights.so_what: Lower migration labor lowers the barrier to GPU analytics adoption, supporting NVIDIA's non-AI-training GPU demand.
